name: Cities, Settlement, and Housing
summary: Named cities with coordinates for the Atlas, the distributed capital, urban design standards, tenure and housing cost, homelessness, and subsea stations.

settlement.policy: More cities rather than bigger cities: a settlement pattern with a few dominant nodes has a small number of very expensive failure modes.

distributedCapital.rationale: A capital is a single point of failure, and so is a capital's political culture.

cities.name: Sennary

twentyMinuteStandard.name: The twenty-minute standard
twentyMinuteStandard.summary: Every dwelling within 20 civil minutes on foot or cycle of a health post, school, library, food market, green space, and transit stop. A Concord floor, audited per Commune.

buildingStandards.adaptabilityRationale: A dwelling is expected to hold different numbers of people at different points in a 150-year life; Elysians move house far less often than Earth populations and reconfigure far more.
buildingStandards.accessibilityRationale: 710 million Elysians are over 100 EY and home-first healthcare depends on dwellings a frail person can be cared for in.

land.purpose: The building depreciates and is maintained; the land's value accrues to the Commune that created it.

subseaStations.canonNote: Stations, not cities. No Elysian settlement of any size exists underwater, no one is born in one, and the Concord has never proposed subsea urbanisation. Living permanently below the sea is regarded as an expensive answer to a question nobody has.

tenure.name: Cooperative and mutual housing
tenure.summary: Members hold a right of occupancy rather than a tradeable asset, pay cost rent, and recover contributions indexed to construction costs rather than land values, so nobody profits from the shortage.

tenure.name: Private rented
tenure.summary: Indefinite tenancies by default, indexed rent caps, eviction only for specified cause through a court, and landlord licensing.

reasons: land value tax removes most speculative return
supply is permitted and District duty is justiciable

homelessness.canonNote: Rare, brief, and non-punitive, and not eliminated. The residual is a problem of illness and autonomy that the housing system cannot solve alone.

specialProvision.name: Housing on release from custody
specialProvision.summary: Guaranteed and arranged before release, not applied for after.

specialProvision.name: Managed retreat replacement
specialProvision.summary: Full replacement value with the Commune relocated together where residents choose.

specialProvision.name: Emergency housing capacity
specialProvision.summary: Held at District level for 4% of District population and exercised annually.

specialProvision.name: Frailty adaptation
specialProvision.summary: Funded on assessment rather than on means, delivered within 45 days in 88% of cases.

knownWeaknesses.name: The twenty-minute standard is not universal
knownWeaknesses.summary: The 5.9% shortfall concentrates in older Elandric quarters and Aurorian settlements too small to support the services.

knownWeaknesses.name: Housing wealth still accumulates
knownWeaknesses.summary: Leasehold and land value tax slow appreciation without stopping it; housing remains a principal driver of the flat wealth Gini.

knownWeaknesses.name: Heritage against density
knownWeaknesses.summary: Communes hold real power over their own built form and some use it to prevent density the Region needs; there is no override and canon does not propose one.

knownWeaknesses.name: Retreat lines are contested
knownWeaknesses.summary: A published retreat line lowers property value the day it is drawn; three Regions have litigated their own lines.

knownWeaknesses.name: Small-settlement viability
knownWeaknesses.summary: Below about 8,000 residents a settlement cannot support the full Commune service set; 6,100 settlements are subsidised to remain viable.

knownWeaknesses.name: Sennary is unloved
knownWeaknesses.summary: A capital nobody has a reason to move to is also a capital nobody knows; Concord-tier remoteness is partly architectural.

knownWeaknesses.name: Homelessness is not zero
knownWeaknesses.summary: 94,000 people homeless for over a year; a health and autonomy problem the housing system cannot reach.

knownWeaknesses.name: District duty is unevenly enforced
knownWeaknesses.summary: The right is only as strong as a person's willingness to litigate, and take-up is lowest among those most affected.

knownWeaknesses.name: Cooperative entry is rationed
knownWeaknesses.summary: The cheapest tenure has waiting lists averaging 2.4 Elysian years, and entry favours those with existing connections.

knownWeaknesses.name: Adaptation delays
knownWeaknesses.summary: 12% wait beyond 45 days, concentrated in Regions with the oldest populations and thinnest administrations.

knownWeaknesses.name: Rural housing quality
knownWeaknesses.summary: Pre-standard housing concentrates in small Aurorian and Veydran settlements where replacement is uneconomic and subsidy has not closed the gap.
